summary: 24-year-old man with ileocolonic Crohn’s on adalimumab and azathioprine: 5 days RIF pain, fever 38.7, tender mass; CT 4.5 cm ileocaecal abscess. IV antibiotics and percutaneous drainage, hold the biologic, avoid systemic steroids with an undrained abscess, then plan (delayed) ileocaecal resection.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right lower abdominal pain and fever
inputs.hpi: Ileocolonic Crohn’s disease diagnosed at 19, on adalimumab and azathioprine. Five days of worsening right lower abdominal pain, fevers and sweats, off food. Bowels loose 3 times a day, no blood. Lost 3 kg.

exam.abdomen: Tender, firm 6 cm mass in the right iliac fossa with localised guarding; no generalised peritonism.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Thickened terminal ileum (25 cm) with a 4.5 × 4 cm rim-enhancing ileocaecal abscess. No free gas. No obstruction.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Crohn’s disease with ileocaecal abscess
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Ileocolonic Crohn’s disease complicated by a 4.5 cm ileocaecal abscess, on adalimumab and azathioprine. IV antibiotics and percutaneous drainage; hold biologic; avoid steroids.

mustNotAlarm.note: The CT report says "No free gas"; a pneumoperitoneum/emergency-laparotomy alarm is a false positive from negated text.
mustNotAlarm.proposedFix: Add negation handling to hasRadResult (no/without/absent … free gas/free air).

mustInclude.note: ECCO 2020: intra-abdominal abscess → antibiotics and percutaneous drainage where feasible, then elective resection.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: The crohns_disease protocol says "Abscess or fistula — urgent imaging and intervention" (red flag) but no step for percutaneous drainage; the management panel shows the appendicitis protocol because PANE ranks appendicitis first (0.71).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add "intra-abdominal abscess: IV antibiotics + percutaneous drainage, then delayed resection; wean steroids" to the crohns_disease protocol (ECCO 2020).

mustInclude.note: Systemic (IV) antibiotics for the abscess in the documented plan for the confirmed diagnosis; oral metronidazole for perianal disease suppression does not count, nor does the appendicitis panel shown because PANE ranks appendicitis first.

mustExclude.note: A Crohn’s ileocaecal abscess is drained, then resected electively (ileocaecal resection); an emergency appendicectomy is the wrong operation.
Systemic corticosteroids with an undrained intra-abdominal abscess increase septic and post-operative complications (ECCO 2020).
mustExclude.knownGapNote: The crohns_disease protocol medications (prednisolone, budesonide, IV hydrocortisone "flare induction") are offered unconditionally, including for a septic abscess.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Condition the Crohn’s steroid medications on "no abscess/sepsis" and add an explicit caution (ECCO 2020).

guideline.name: ECCO guidelines on therapeutics in Crohn’s disease — surgical treatment
guideline.section: Intra-abdominal abscess: antibiotics + percutaneous drainage, then delayed resection; steroids increase post-operative complications and should be weaned before surgery
guideline.citation: Adamina M, Bonovas S, Raine T, et al. ECCO guidelines on therapeutics in Crohn’s disease: surgical treatment. J Crohns Colitis. 2020;14:155–168.

guideline.name: BSG consensus guidelines — management of inflammatory bowel disease in adults
guideline.section: Exclude abscess before starting or continuing anti-TNF; drain sepsis first
guideline.citation: Lamb CA, Kennedy NA, Raine T, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology consensus guidelines on the management of inflammatory bowel disease in adults. Gut. 2019;68(Suppl 3):s1–s106.

rationale: Base Crohn’s case: penetrating disease with an abscess on imaging, on a biologic and a thiopurine. The critical risk is a flare plan (steroids) applied to a septic complication.

authoring.author: Claude (colorectal/anorectal cluster)
